clue.text: Frank is backing endless recent revelling

indicators.note: backing means the little word is is read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written before the turn

indicators.note: revelling suggests wild partying, so these letters are jumbled about
endless means the final letter of recent is cut off

explanation.surface: Someone candid admits to recent bouts of carousing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns IS into SI; 'endless' trims recent to RECEN and 'revelling' rearranges that into NCERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a frank person speaks openly and without pretence, which is being truthful in what one says.

clue.text: Trapped gases in trendy beer

parts.note: something trendy is said to be in

indicators.note: in places the gas symbols inside the word for beer

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
H and O are the chemical symbols of hydrogen and oxygen, both gases

explanation.surface: Fizzy gases are captured inside a fashionable beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gases' gives two element symbols, H for hydrogen and O for oxygen, rather than any word for gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to be stuck in a hole is to be cornered in a difficult situation with no easy way out.

clue.text: Conservative Party and AA joiners do it

parts.note: a rave is a large dance party

explanation.surface: Tories and members of the Automobile Association both throw parties.
explanation.walkthrough: AA here is Alcoholics Anonymous, not the British motoring organisation the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic hint: people joining Alcoholics Anonymous typically long desperately for a drink they must give up.

clue.text: Con brio avoided by bass, with good reason

indicators.note: avoided by means the bass abbreviation is dropped from the musical direction

parts.note: con brio is the musical direction meaning with vigour, i.e. brightly
B is the abbreviation for bass in music

explanation.surface: A musical direction to play with spirit is ignored by the bass section, and justifiably.
explanation.walkthrough: Con brio, Italian for 'with spirit', is rendered as BRIGHTLY; losing B leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something done with justification is done correctly and properly, as one ought.

clue.text: Powerful stuff adult left out of Bible

parts.note: A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: out of places the word for left outside the Bible abbreviation

parts.note: to quit is to have left
AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: A strong drink is talked of as adult material dropped from scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a direction or a remainder, but it is the past tense of quit; 'out of' then says that word sits outside the Bible version.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: the Scandinavian caraway spirit is strong liquor, so potent drink.

clue.text: Downs no-frills fruit drink, swallowing very loudly

indicators.note: swallowing means the trimmed drink takes the loudness marking inside itself
no-frills means the drink loses its outer edges, first and last letters

parts.note: squash is a British concentrated fruit drink diluted with water
FF is fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Someone gulps a basic fruit drink, slurping noisily.
explanation.walkthrough: Squash is a British cordial diluted with water; 'no-frills' takes off both its ends before the loudness marking goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to down a drink is to swallow it in big gulps, the verb in the same form.

clue.text: A pig swilling its mother's water

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal
swine is another word for pig

explanation.surface: A piglet slurps up water belonging to its sow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swilling' only colours the surface; the mother of a farm animal is its dam, a breeding term.
explanation.definitionFit: Jocular phrase: the first man had only plain drinking water to drink, so the humorous name means water.

clue.text: Cracking vessel in charge of German one

parts.note: IC is the usual abbreviation for in charge
an E-boat was a German torpedo boat in the Second World War, one being a vessel

explanation.surface: A splendid ship is commanded by a German sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracking' looks like praise but describes breaking ice; 'one' refers back to vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a boat built to break through frozen sea is a vessel that cracks its way along.

clue.text: Roman saw visitor with Vienna rolls

indicators.note: rolls suggests tumbling, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A visitor to Austria's capital eats bread rolls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' is a noun, a saying, not the past tense of see.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin proverb 'in wine, truth' is an old Roman saying, and a saw is a proverb.

clue.text: A short break over wine

indicators.note: over means the pieces are turned over, read backwards

parts.note: vac is short for vacation, a break

explanation.surface: A brief holiday is spent drinking wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Spanish sparkling wine is a kind of wine.

clue.text: In pubs, golf chum describes favourite holes-in-one

indicators.note: describes in the sense of drawing round, so the golf letter and chum go around favourite

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a pal is a chum
the in thing is the favourite
a hole-in-one in golf is called an ace

explanation.surface: Over drinks, a golfing friend recounts his favourite holes-in-one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describes' means encircles, as a geometer describes a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: gin palaces were showy Victorian bars, a kind of public house.

clue.text: He's not intoxicated, I swear

indicators.note: intoxicated means drunk, so the letters reel about

explanation.surface: A man protests that he is sober.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in He's is ignored, leaving seven letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Interjection: 'honest!' is said to vouch for one's truthfulness, as is 'I swear'.

clue.text: Popular music style for tea perhaps

parts.note: popular things are in
fusion is a style blending jazz with rock or other genres

explanation.surface: A trendy musical genre is said to be suitable for tea time.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: tea is made by steeping leaves in hot water, a classic brew of that type.

clue.text: Crew enjoys working to eject new drink supplier

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are put to work in a new order
to eject means one letter is thrown out of the mix

explanation.surface: A ship's company enjoys work but throws out a newcomer.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange CREW ENJOYS less N, removed by 'to eject'.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: this dairy breed from the Channel Islands supplies milk, so it provides a drink.

clue.text: Fixes remarkable Irish architect's tool

parts.note: to set is to fix in place
quare is an Irish dialect word for remarkable or strange

explanation.surface: An Irish architect mends a notable instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: QUARE is Irish English for odd or remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the triangular drawing instrument is used by draughtsmen and architects for right angles.

clue.text: Output of 14? Secretary drinks it about noon

indicators.note: drinks means the secretary takes in what follows

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

indicators.note: about means the little word it goes round the noon letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An office assistant downs a drink around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 14 is the Jersey cow; its output is milk, and the answer is British slang for a pint of milk.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross-reference: a dairy cow produces milk, and the slang term is a pint of milk.

clue.text: Mating time in the Highlands primarily? Nothing wrong with that

indicators.note: in places the mating period inside the two initials
primarily picks the first letters of the words

parts.note: the rut is the mating season of deer

explanation.surface: Deer mate in the Scottish Highlands, and there's nothing wrong with that.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: something wholly accurate contains no falsehood, so there is nothing wrong in it.

clue.text: He's pragmatic dealing with biggest stars

parts.note: re means concerning or dealing with
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: A sensible agent handles only top celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a pragmatic person accepts things as they are, a practical down-to-earth type.

clue.text: Job for some setters about a quarter to five, in case

parts.note: re means about

indicators.note: in places the short run inside the court case

parts.note: a trial is a court case

indicators.note: to means the quarter letter is placed up against the numeral that follows

parts.note: E, east, is one of the four compass quarters
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Crossword compilers are busy about a quarter to five on a case.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters are the gundogs, not crossword compilers; EV (a quarter to five) goes inside TRIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: setters are gun dogs trained to point at and bring back shot game, which is fetching work.

clue.text: How climbers may look, sore everywhere at summit of Eiger?

indicators.note: everywhere suggests scattering, so the letters are spread into a new order
summit of picks the top, i.e. first, letter in a down clue

explanation.surface: Mountaineers ache all over on reaching the top of the Eiger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbers' are also climbing roses, which may look pink; the Eiger is a Swiss peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: rosy pink is the colour of many climbing roses, and of mountaineers flushed with effort.

clue.text: Spectator contributor is spiking special feature

indicators.note: spiking means the little word is driven into the feature

parts.note: an add-on is an extra feature
taken as written

explanation.surface: A magazine columnist is adding something to a drink for a special piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spectator was Joseph Addison and Richard Steele's 1711 daily, not today's magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Joseph Addison, the essayist, co-founded and wrote for the original Spectator.

clue.text: Unearth papers about complaint

indicators.note: about means the papers abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: ID, identity papers
gout is a medical complaint

explanation.surface: Someone digs out documents concerning a medical complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to unearth something is to find it by searching, the same verb sense.

clue.text: Welsh guy who in Paris guzzles Irish cocktail

parts.note: Dai is a common Welsh man's name

indicators.note: guzzles means the French word swallows the Irish abbreviation

parts.note: qui is French for who

explanation.surface: A Welshman in Paris knocks back an Irish cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the rum, lime and sugar mix is a classic mixed drink.

clue.text: Ingredients of withdrawn drink

indicators.note: of in the sense of made of, the reserved word holding the joining word

parts.note: a shy person is withdrawn
a recipe's ingredients are listed with and between them, as in beer and lemonade

explanation.surface: A shy person's drink has a list of ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ingredients' stands for the joining word in a recipe list such as beer and lemonade, which are this drink's own two components.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: beer mixed with lemonade is a long drink.

clue.text: Enjoy getting stripped, tucking into golden wine

indicators.note: tucking into means the stripped word goes inside the gold symbol

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: stripped means losing the outer letters, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a striptease while drinking a golden wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting stripped' takes the outer letters off Enjoy to leave NJO.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Loire region gives its name to its white and rosé wines.

clue.text: Cocktail priest takes in a soft drink with old man

parts.note: cola is a fizzy soft drink
da is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A priest invites in a lad for a soft drink with his father.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the rum, coconut and pineapple mix is a well-known mixed drink.

clue.text: Gravy train's beginning at this very instant

parts.note: jus is a thin gravy, from the French for juice

indicators.note: beginning picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: The start of the gravy train is happening right now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gravy train' is a phrase about easy money, but here it splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: 'just' as in 'just now' means at this very moment.

clue.text: Spread around most of the goodness

parts.note: to strew is to scatter or spread around

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the word is dropped

explanation.surface: Kindness is shared widely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goodness' is the exclamation, not virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: Exclamation: both are mild Australian- and British-style cries of surprise, interchangeable as oaths.

clue.text: G9 clashed with EU for real

indicators.note: clashed means the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: G and the number nine written out

explanation.surface: A group of nine nations quarrelled with the European Union.
explanation.walkthrough: Read G9 as G followed by NINE, then mix with EU.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something authentic is real rather than fake.
